standards.name: HTTP and REST verbs
standards.rule: GET reads, POST creates, PATCH changes part of a resource; the URL names a thing, not an action.
standards.why: Every developer and every tool already knows what the verbs mean.

standards.name: HTTP status codes
standards.rule: 200 read, 201 created, 400 bad input, 404 not found, 502 a service is unreachable, 504 a service is too slow.
standards.why: The caller can react to the number without reading the text.

standards.name: JSON bodies
standards.rule: Requests and responses are JSON with the content type application/json.
standards.why: JSON is readable, small, and every language can parse it.

standards.name: UTF-8 text
standards.why: Names such as Muñoz or Dela Cruz arrive unchanged.

standards.name: ISO 8601 dates
standards.rule: Dates are written year-month-day with a four digit year.
standards.why: 04/03/2027 is 4 March in one country and 3 April in another.

standards.name: ISO 4217 currency codes
standards.rule: A currency is a three-letter code next to the amount.
standards.why: 500 alone could be pesos or dollars.

standards.name: OpenAPI 3
standards.rule: The API is described in an OpenAPI 3 file, and every operation lists the requirements it satisfies.
standards.why: One file is the contract, the documentation, and the list of endpoints to test.

standards.name: One error format
standards.why: Callers write one error handler, and the message is plain language.

standards.name: Timeouts
standards.rule: Every call to another system has a timeout of 800 ms, so 3 tries and our own work fit in 3000 ms.
standards.why: Without a timeout one slow system makes everything slow.

standards.name: Idempotent retries
standards.rule: Retry only calls that are safe to repeat (GET, or a POST with a request number); at most 3 attempts.
standards.why: A retried payment must not be paid twice.

standards.name: Version in the URL
standards.rule: The plain /api is version 1. A change that breaks callers appears under /api/v2, and the old one stays for a while.
standards.why: Existing callers keep working while new ones move.

standards.name: No secrets in code
standards.rule: Keys and passwords come from environment variables, never from a file in the repository.
standards.why: Whatever is in the repository is public history.
